title: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison) - physician decides. CLL/SLL pathway: presentation -> workup -> Rai/Binet staging -> iwCLL treatment indication (watch-and-wait vs treat) -> TP53 (del(17p)/TP53) and IGHV risk stratification -> first-line targeted therapy (covalent/non-covalent BTKi vs venetoclax-obinutuzumab vs select chemoimmunotherapy) -> surveillance -> relapsed/refractory pathway by prior therapy class and Richter transformation. Structural pathway only; no proprietary guideline text reproduced, no doses invented. No existing StewardMD dose protocol matched CLL agents, so treatment leaves give checklist guidance without doses. DRAFT - not clinically activated; the physician decides.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with standard oncology references (NCCN / iwCLL / DeVita / Harrison). No dose regimens are asserted; agents are named as classes for clinician selection.

a.text: iwCLL active-disease (treatment) indications include progressive marrow failure (worsening anemia or thrombocytopenia), massive or progressive/symptomatic splenomegaly or lymphadenopathy, progressive lymphocytosis with a short doubling time, autoimmune cytopenia poorly responsive to steroids, or constitutional symptoms. Absolute lymphocyte count alone is not an indication.

b.text: Test del(17p) by FISH and TP53 by sequencing before every line of therapy. TP53-aberrant disease responds poorly to chemoimmunotherapy; use targeted agents (BTK inhibitor or venetoclax-based).

c.text: Venetoclax requires tumor-lysis-syndrome risk stratification, a weekly dose ramp-up, and hydration; monitor labs closely during escalation.

d.text: IGHV mutation status is stable over the disease course; test once. IGHV-unmutated disease has shorter benefit from chemoimmunotherapy and generally favors targeted therapy.

nodes.name: Presentation
nodes.title: CLL / SLL: presentation
nodes.description: Management branches first by presentation. Choose the applicable scenario.
bullets: Newly diagnosed CLL or SLL (tissue-equivalent small lymphocytic lymphoma)
Previously treated, now relapsed or refractory
Sudden clinical deterioration - suspect Richter (histologic) transformation

nodes.name: Workup
nodes.title: Diagnostic workup
nodes.description: Confirm the diagnosis and establish baseline disease burden and biology.
bullets: History and physical; palpate all nodal areas, liver and spleen; note B-symptoms and performance status
CBC with differential and peripheral smear (smudge cells); confirm clonal B-lymphocytosis >= 5 x 10^9/L for CLL
Flow-cytometry immunophenotype: CD19+ CD5+ CD23+, dim surface immunoglobulin, kappa/lambda restriction
SLL if nodal/tissue disease without the required blood lymphocytosis (lymph-node biopsy)
Prognostic testing: FISH panel (del(13q), trisomy 12, del(11q), del(17p)), TP53 sequencing, IGHV mutation status

bullets.label: Baseline labs
bullets.sub: LDH, beta-2-microglobulin, comprehensive metabolic panel, immunoglobulins, DAT, hepatitis B/C and HIV serology before therapy

nodes.name: Staging
nodes.title: Clinical staging (Rai / Binet)
nodes.description: Assign a clinical stage; staging with prognostic markers frames the treatment-indication decision.

nodes.name: Treatment indication
nodes.title: iwCLL treatment indication: watch-and-wait vs treat
nodes.description: Early-stage asymptomatic CLL is observed; treatment starts only when active-disease (iwCLL) criteria are met. There is no survival benefit to treating asymptomatic early disease.

nodes.name: Watch-and-wait
nodes.title: Active surveillance (watch-and-wait)
nodes.description: Observation with periodic monitoring until an iwCLL treatment indication develops.
bullets: History, exam and CBC every 3-6 months (individualize by pace of disease)
Reassess for iwCLL indications at each visit; check the lymphocyte doubling time
Age-appropriate infection prophylaxis and vaccinations (avoid live vaccines); annual influenza, pneumococcal, COVID and zoster (non-live)
No routine CT imaging in asymptomatic patients; investigate new or progressive symptoms
Begin therapy when active-disease criteria are met
nodes.linkLabel: When active-disease criteria develop: re-enter the treatment-indication step

nodes.name: TP53 status
nodes.title: Risk stratification: del(17p) / TP53
nodes.description: Before first-line therapy, stratify by TP53 status. TP53 aberration (del(17p) and/or TP53 mutation) is the dominant adverse marker and steers away from chemoimmunotherapy.

tables.title: Key first-line prognostic markers
rows: Adverse; targeted therapy overcomes much of the risk

nodes.name: TP53-aberrant regimen
nodes.title: First-line, TP53-aberrant: targeted regimen choice
nodes.description: TP53-aberrant CLL is treated with continuous BTK inhibition or fixed-duration venetoclax-based therapy; chemoimmunotherapy is not used.

nodes.name: TP53 aberrant - BTKi
nodes.title: First-line TP53-aberrant: continuous BTK inhibitor
nodes.description: A covalent second-generation BTK inhibitor is preferred for its cardiovascular tolerability; continue until progression or intolerance.
bullets: Covalent BTK inhibitor (acalabrutinib or zanubrutinib preferred over ibrutinib for atrial fibrillation and hypertension risk)
Continuous therapy until progression or unacceptable toxicity
Baseline and on-treatment cardiovascular review (blood pressure, atrial fibrillation, bleeding risk); reconcile anticoagulants and CYP3A interactions
This is a preferred option even with TP53 aberration (activity is largely independent of TP53)

nodes.name: TP53 aberrant - VenO
nodes.title: First-line TP53-aberrant: venetoclax-obinutuzumab (fixed duration)
nodes.description: Fixed-duration venetoclax with obinutuzumab is an option offering a time-limited, chemotherapy-free course.
bullets: Venetoclax with obinutuzumab, given as a fixed-duration (approximately 12-month) course
Mandatory tumor-lysis-syndrome risk assessment, hydration and weekly venetoclax dose ramp-up
Obinutuzumab: infusion-reaction premedication and hepatitis B reactivation prophylaxis if HBcAb-positive
Durable remissions are shorter with TP53 aberration than in TP53 wild-type disease - plan close follow-up

nodes.name: IGHV status
nodes.title: TP53 wild-type: IGHV mutation status
nodes.description: In TP53 wild-type disease, IGHV mutation status refines first-line options - specifically whether time-limited chemoimmunotherapy remains reasonable.

nodes.name: IGHV-unmutated regimen
nodes.title: First-line, TP53-WT / IGHV-unmutated: regimen choice
nodes.description: IGHV-unmutated disease favors targeted therapy over chemoimmunotherapy; choose continuous BTK inhibition or fixed-duration venetoclax-obinutuzumab.

nodes.name: IGHV-unmut - BTKi
nodes.title: First-line IGHV-unmutated: continuous BTK inhibitor
nodes.description: Continuous covalent BTK inhibition, preferred class for the tolerability profile.
bullets: Covalent BTK inhibitor (acalabrutinib or zanubrutinib preferred over ibrutinib)
Continuous until progression or intolerance
Cardiovascular and bleeding surveillance; manage drug interactions
Avoid chemoimmunotherapy given the short benefit in IGHV-unmutated disease

nodes.name: IGHV-unmut - VenO
nodes.title: First-line IGHV-unmutated: venetoclax-obinutuzumab (fixed duration)
nodes.description: Fixed-duration chemotherapy-free option with high rates of undetectable measurable residual disease.
bullets: Venetoclax + obinutuzumab, fixed-duration (approximately 12 months)
Tumor-lysis prophylaxis with staged venetoclax ramp-up
Hepatitis B reactivation prophylaxis with the anti-CD20 antibody
Time-limited course is attractive; IGHV-unmutated remissions run shorter than IGHV-mutated

nodes.name: IGHV-mutated regimen
nodes.title: First-line, TP53-WT / IGHV-mutated: regimen choice
nodes.description: Targeted therapy is preferred, but time-limited chemoimmunotherapy remains a reasonable option for fit, younger IGHV-mutated patients who prefer a finite course.

nodes.name: IGHV-mut - BTKi
nodes.title: First-line IGHV-mutated: continuous BTK inhibitor
nodes.description: Continuous covalent BTK inhibition.
bullets: Covalent BTK inhibitor (acalabrutinib or zanubrutinib preferred)
Continuous until progression or intolerance
Cardiovascular / bleeding monitoring and interaction review

nodes.name: IGHV-mut - VenO
nodes.title: First-line IGHV-mutated: venetoclax-obinutuzumab (fixed duration)
nodes.description: Fixed-duration chemotherapy-free therapy; IGHV-mutated disease achieves particularly durable remissions.
bullets: Venetoclax + obinutuzumab, fixed-duration (approximately 12 months)
Tumor-lysis prophylaxis and staged ramp-up
Hepatitis B reactivation prophylaxis with the anti-CD20 antibody

nodes.name: IGHV-mut - CIT
nodes.title: First-line IGHV-mutated: chemoimmunotherapy (select patients)
nodes.description: Time-limited chemoimmunotherapy remains an option only in young, fit, TP53-WT / IGHV-mutated patients; targeted therapy is otherwise preferred.
bullets: Fit patient: fludarabine-cyclophosphamide-rituximab (FCR) can give long remissions in IGHV-mutated disease
Less fit / older: bendamustine-rituximab (BR)
Only if TP53 wild-type; never use chemoimmunotherapy with del(17p) / TP53 mutation
Counsel on infection risk, cytopenias, and a small risk of therapy-related myeloid neoplasm; targeted therapy is the preferred alternative

nodes.name: Supportive care
nodes.title: Supportive care during / after therapy
nodes.description: Supportive-care measures apply across all first-line regimens.
bullets: Infection prophylaxis per regimen (antiviral, and PJP prophylaxis with purine-analog or steroid exposure)
Vaccinate (non-live); avoid live vaccines; expect blunted responses on anti-CD20 therapy
Manage treatment-emergent autoimmune cytopenias; recognize tumor flare / lymphocytosis with BTK inhibitors
Tumor-lysis monitoring during venetoclax ramp-up; cardiovascular monitoring on BTK inhibitors

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Response assessment and surveillance
nodes.description: Assess response and follow after first-line therapy.
bullets: Assess response by iwCLL criteria (exam, CBC); routine marrow and CT only if needed to confirm complete remission or clarify cytopenias
Follow-up history, exam and CBC every 3-6 months
Watch for autoimmune cytopenias and second cancers (skin surveillance)
At clinical relapse, re-test del(17p)/TP53 and re-stage before choosing next-line therapy
nodes.linkLabel: On relapse: enter the relapsed / refractory pathway

nodes.name: Relapse workup
nodes.title: Relapsed / refractory: reassessment
nodes.description: At relapse, re-confirm progression and repeat molecular testing; exclude Richter transformation before selecting therapy.
bullets: Confirm progression by iwCLL criteria; distinguish true progression from BTK-inhibitor tumor flare
Repeat FISH del(17p) and TP53 sequencing (clonal evolution is common at relapse)
Assess for Richter transformation: rapid nodal growth, high LDH, B-symptoms, discordant PET avidity -> biopsy the most avid site
Review the prior regimen, response depth and duration, and reason for stopping (progression vs intolerance)

nodes.name: Prior therapy
nodes.title: Relapsed / refractory: prior therapy class
nodes.description: Next-line therapy is chosen to switch mechanism relative to the prior regimen.

options.label: Progressed on / after a covalent BTK inhibitor

nodes.name: After BTKi
nodes.title: Relapse after a covalent BTK inhibitor: next class
nodes.description: After progression on a covalent BTK inhibitor, switch mechanism to venetoclax-based therapy, a non-covalent BTK inhibitor, or cellular therapy in multiply-refractory disease.

nodes.name: Venetoclax after BTKi
nodes.title: Post-BTKi: venetoclax-based therapy
nodes.description: Switching to venetoclax (with or without an anti-CD20 antibody) after covalent BTK-inhibitor failure.
bullets: Venetoclax +/- rituximab; effective after BTK-inhibitor progression (non-cross-resistant mechanism)
Tumor-lysis risk assessment and weekly ramp-up
Consider continuous vs fixed-duration by prior exposure and remission depth

nodes.name: Non-covalent BTKi
nodes.title: Post-BTKi: non-covalent BTK inhibitor
nodes.description: A non-covalent (reversible) BTK inhibitor retains activity after covalent BTK-inhibitor failure, including with BTK C481 resistance mutations.
bullets: Non-covalent BTK inhibitor (e.g. pirtobrutinib) - active after covalent BTK-inhibitor progression or intolerance
Useful bridge when venetoclax is unsuitable or already used
Continue until progression or intolerance

nodes.name: Cellular therapy
nodes.title: Double-refractory: CAR-T / allogeneic transplant
nodes.description: For disease refractory to both BTK inhibitors and venetoclax, consider cellular therapy in appropriate candidates.
bullets: CD19 CAR-T is an option for BTK-inhibitor and venetoclax double-refractory CLL in fit patients
Allogeneic transplant for selected younger, fit patients with high-risk refractory disease
Enroll on a clinical trial where available
Coordinate at a cellular-therapy / transplant center

nodes.name: After venetoclax
nodes.title: Relapse after fixed-duration venetoclax
nodes.description: After a fixed-duration venetoclax course, options depend on remission duration and prior BTK-inhibitor exposure.
bullets: BTK inhibitor (covalent if BTK-inhibitor-naive; otherwise non-covalent) as the mechanism switch
Venetoclax retreatment is reasonable after a long remission from a prior fixed-duration course
Re-test TP53; consider CAR-T / transplant if also BTK-inhibitor-refractory
Clinical trial where available
nodes.linkLabel: If also BTK-inhibitor-refractory: consider cellular therapy

nodes.name: After chemoimmunotherapy
nodes.title: Relapse after chemoimmunotherapy
nodes.description: After prior chemoimmunotherapy, switch to targeted therapy; do not repeat chemoimmunotherapy.
bullets: Continuous covalent BTK inhibitor, or fixed-duration venetoclax +/- rituximab
Choose by comorbidity, prior toxicity and patient preference for continuous vs time-limited therapy
Re-test del(17p)/TP53 - clonal evolution is common after chemoimmunotherapy
Avoid re-treating with chemoimmunotherapy

nodes.name: Richter workup
nodes.title: Suspected Richter transformation: workup
nodes.description: Confirm transformation histologically before changing strategy - the treatment and prognosis differ sharply from CLL.
bullets: PET-CT to identify the most metabolically avid site (high SUV suggests transformation)
Excisional or core biopsy of the most avid node to confirm diffuse large B-cell (or, rarely, Hodgkin) histology
Establish clonal relationship to the CLL where feasible (clonally related disease carries a worse prognosis)
Baseline staging, LDH, and performance status

nodes.name: Richter transformation
nodes.title: Richter transformation: treatment
nodes.description: Biopsy-proven aggressive-lymphoma transformation is treated as high-grade lymphoma, ideally on a clinical trial.
bullets: Treat the diffuse large B-cell histology with anthracycline-based immunochemotherapy (e.g. R-CHOP-type)
Prioritize a clinical trial given poor outcomes with standard chemotherapy
Consider consolidation with allogeneic (or autologous) transplant in responders who are fit
Hodgkin-variant transformation is treated with Hodgkin-lymphoma-directed therapy
Manage the underlying CLL and provide supportive / infection prophylaxis
